title: SO2 count spread gave no clear common change in 49 invertebrate records from 1981-2003 papers
abstract: We tested whether SO2 changed invertebrate count spread relative to the mean. We used 49 records from 11 papers published in 1981-2003, with equal paper weights. The geometric variance-to-mean ratio was 1.23, with a conditional 95 percent interval of 0.54 to 2.82. Sample-size and field exclusions gave estimates below one, with intervals that included one. Every single-paper omission interval included one. Two of four European region-period cells had only one paper. Thus the extract did not establish a common spread change or a strong repeated regional and period pattern. This extends a prior ozone spread test to different pollutant records. The source archive overlaps a prior SO2 mean analysis. Selected studies, mixed sampling units, reconstructed errors, co-pollutants and shared programmes limit inference. Climate and weather interactions were not tested. We provide code, source hashes, aggregate results, a figure and independent arithmetic checks.

display.caption: SO2 count spread estimates. Available European cell intervals use four-test correction. Other intervals are conditional 95 percent limits. Sparse cells are not shown.

citations.reason: Independent-pollutant extension of its ozone spread analysis; same source review, different papers.
Inherits count labels and period split, then excludes transformed measurements and tests spread rather than mean.
